author: reek
body: A Count-Min sketch works because its rows are INDEPENDENT hash functions. Every key is counted once per row, a query takes the minimum across rows, and the minimum is a good estimate precisely because a key that collides with something in one row is unlikely to collide in another. Correlate the rows and the minimum stops helping: the same pairs collide everywhere, so the error the structure exists to bound is simply not bounded.

author: reek
body: The measurement is the structure's own promise. Insert N distinct keys with a count of one each into a sketch wide enough to hold them comfortably, then ask for every key back. A sketch whose rows are independent answers one almost every time. A sketch whose rows agree with each other overestimates, because a collision in row zero is a collision in every row.

author: reek
body: Every key was inserted exactly once, so every honest estimate is one. Count how many come back exact, and record the worst overestimate.

author: reek
body: How many distinct columns each row actually uses. Independent rows spread over the width; correlated rows crowd into the same few columns, and the second row looking like the first is the defect stated directly.
